Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  August 6, 2026

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on August 6, 2026. Commissioner Denmon
called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Ashley Ferrette announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Sofia
  Quinones - District 2 Commissioner Alex Monge - District 3,
  Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at Large
  Vacant:  District 4

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Teresa Estrada  Assistant Director
  Anthony Harris  Recreation Supervisor
  Geoffrey Okamoto  Human Services Transportation Manager
  Joel Ruelas  Park Maintenance Supervisor
  Ashley Ferrette  Staff Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. Commissioner Denmon went on the record to correct the date of the May
minutes approval, which was previously listed as May 5, 2026, but was incorrect. Staff
Assistant Ashley Ferrette also stated for the record that the correct date for the agenda
was May 7, 2026, rather than May 5, 2026.

It was moved by Commissioner Brown and second by Commissioner Monge that the
minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on August 7, 2025, be
approved. The following roll call vote carried the motion:
Ayes: Commissioner Denmon, and Commissioner Quinones
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Park Maintenance Supervisor Joel Ruelas reported
the following: Parks Division - This past week, fencing was installed around the baseball
fields at Rogers Park in preparation for the upcoming renovation project. Construction of
the Siminski Park Community Garden is scheduled to begin shortly. Improvements at North

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

Park, including the installation of a new gazebo and upgraded play equipment, are
scheduled to begin following the Chili Cook-Off on August 15th. Graffiti Division - The
Graffiti Abatement staff painted the light poles and tree planters at the public parking
areas along Manchester from 2nd Avenue to 12th Avenue and at the Morningside Library.
In July, the Darby-Dixon neighborhood in Council District 4, as well as the area surrounding
Edward Vincent Park in Council District 1, experienced heavy graffiti activity and required
extensive abatement efforts. Tree Division – WCA is wrapping up this fiscal year’s annual
tree trimming. They have started on several end of the year projects to wrap up this year’s
budget which include pines and palm trees at Edward Vincent Park along with pines and
palm trees at City Hall. Eucalyptus trees are being trimmed at Rogers and Darby Parks. On
August 7th, city crews will be starting the trimming and skinning of robusta palms on Prairie
Avenue and Century Boulevard.
REPORT - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor Anthony Harris reported the following:
Youth Sports Update - The mission of keeping Inglewood's youth active, engaged, and
connected through sports continues to thrive. Since our last Recreation Commission
meeting, the City of Inglewood Youth Sports League (IYSL) has provided a variety of high-
quality athletic programs and memorable experiences that encourage healthy lifestyles,
skill development, and community involvement for our young residents. Our summer
programming features two exciting opportunities: the inaugural Summer Soccer League
and the ever-popular Dodgers Dream team Baseball/Softball Program. Now in its inaugural
season, the Summer Soccer League was created to provide a natural progression for our
youngest athletes after completing their spring Dodgers Dream team T-Ball and Coach
Pitch Baseball experience. The league introduces fundamental soccer skills while
promoting teamwork, sportsmanship, and confidence. More importantly, it creates
meaningful opportunities for mental, physical, and social development in a fun and
supportive environment. Designed for boys and girls ages 4–6, the league welcomed more
than 100 participants across eight teams. Community members are invited to experience
the excitement firsthand by attending games on Saturday, August 8th, or Wednesday,
August 12th, and cheering on our future stars. Meanwhile, the Dodgers Dreamteam
Summer season continues to be one of our flagship programs, currently serving more than
400 boys and girls ages 9–18. Year after year, participants return because of the
exceptional experience created through our outstanding partnership with the Los Angeles
Dodgers Foundation. Beyond baseball and softball instruction, the program provides
mentorship, character development, leadership opportunities, and valuable life lessons
that extend well beyond the playing field. The summer season concludes on September
5th, when participants from both the Summer Soccer League and Dodgers Dreamteam
Baseball/Softball will celebrate another successful season with individual team award
presentations recognizing their hard work, growth, and accomplishments. As the summer
comes to a close, September also marks the culmination of another outstanding year of

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

youth sports in Inglewood. To commemorate the achievements of our athletes, coaches,
volunteers, and staff, the City of Inglewood Youth Sports League is proud to present the
Inaugural IYSL End of the Year Sports Awards—a premier celebration recognizing
excellence, character, leadership, and dedication throughout the 2025–2026 sports year.
This landmark event brings together participants from every IYSL program for one unified
evening of recognition. While each team traditionally celebrates at the conclusion of its
season, the End of the Year Sports Awards honor those individuals, whose commitment
and contributions have made a lasting impact both on and off the field. Awards will be
presented in the following categories: Most Inspirational Athlete, Leadership Award,
Athlete of the Year, Team Parent of the Year, Volunteer Assistant Coach of the Year,
Volunteer Head Coach of the Year, City Sports Staff Member of the Year, and Athletic
Achievement Award. The celebration will be held on Tuesday, September 1st, at the
Inglewood Senior Center. Early Learners Program - The Park, Recreation and Community
Services Department's Early Learners Play to Learn Program will host an Open House this
Saturday, August 8th. If you know anyone who may be interested in enrolling their child in
our program, we encourage you to invite them to the Open House. It is a great opportunity
for families to tour our classrooms, meet our dedicated staff, learn about our curriculum,
and see firsthand what our program offers. Our Early Learners Play to Learn Program
fosters early childhood development through creative, hands-on learning in a safe,
nurturing, and fun environment. We offer programs tailored to children at various stages
of development, including Parent & Me classes for toddlers 12–29 months, Tiny Tots
classes for children 24–35 months, Early Learners and Spanish Immersion classes for
children 3–5 years. Classes are offered at Rogers Park, Siminski Park, and the Lockhaven
Community Center. We encourage you to share these materials with anyone who may
benefit from this outstanding program. Pilates - The City of Inglewood offers low-impact
mat Pilates classes that strengthen and lengthen the body from the inside out. Pilates is
an excellent way to build core strength, improve muscle tone and posture, increase
flexibility and mobility, and reduce stress—all while delivering a full-body workout suitable
for a wide range of fitness levels. Classes are held Wednesdays: 6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m. at
Rogers Park and Saturdays: 9:00 a.m. – 10:00 a.m. at the Veterans Memorial Building.
During the month of August, we're offering a special promotion. All Saturday Pilates classes
are just $10, which is 50% off the regular class fee. This promotion is designed to introduce
more members of our community to the many benefits of Pilates, and we encourage
everyone to take advantage of this opportunity. Upcoming Special Events - Movies in the
Park - Don’t Miss the Grand Finale of Our Summer Movies in the Park Series! Bring the
whole family for a wild evening of adventure, laughter, and fun under the stars as we wrap
up another incredible season of Summer Movies in the Park! Join us on Saturday, August
15, at North Park for Disney’s Zootopia 2. The festivities begin at 6:00 p.m. with exciting
pre-show activities, including arts and crafts, face painting, and more. The movie will begin
at dusk. Be sure to bring your blankets, lawn chairs, and your favorite snacks, and join us
for one last unforgettable night of family fun under the stars! Hispanic Heritage Festival –

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

The City’s annual Hispanic Heritage Festival will take place on Saturday, September 19,
2026, from 11:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. in downtown Inglewood on Market Street. This exciting
community celebration will feature live entertainment, delicious food, a classic car show,
vendor and community information booths, health screenings, cultural activities, and fun
for the entire family. We encourage everyone to come out and celebrate the rich
traditions, history, and contributions of Hispanic and Latino communities while enjoying a
day of music, culture, and community spirit.

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Transportation Manager Geoffrey Okamoto
reported on the following: Paratransit - The City of Inglewood’s paratransit program
continues to provide trips to seniors and the disabled community in Inglewood and
Hawthorne. Recently a part time bus operator was brought on to help ensure adequate
service levels. Human Services Superintendent attended a Federal Transit Administration
(FTA) workshop on transit worker fatigue, which touched on aspects of performance,
health and safety. The workshop provided best practices for transit agencies to review to
help their agencies improve or at the very least identify aspects of transit worker fatigue.
Finally, our taxi service ASC will be introducing their new EZTransport system, which they
will be transitioning from their current MJM portal. Essentially the new program will
provide the same functionality as the current software provides. The new system is slated
to be in operation on August 1, 2026. The transition is expected be a seamless transition
where customers will not be affected. Despite the recent heatwaves, our paratransit
service has been able to transport its passengers with minimal issues. Elderly Nutrition
Program - The Senior Center proudly serves approximately 460 seniors each week through
both home-delivered meals for homebound individuals and congregate dining services. To
further support our community's nutritional needs, monthly shelf-stable meal boxes are
distributed in collaboration with the Los Angeles Food Bank. Our Nutrition Program has
completed the distribution of Emergency Meals. Emergency Meals are ready-to-eat food
items designed to be on hand in the event of an emergency. We have begun to distribute
Farmers' Market cards, with trips to the market provided by the senior centers
transportation department. In the coming months, we will celebrate with special meals for
occasions such as Labor Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas. Additionally, our
meal program supports seniors on center-organized field trips, ensuring our seniors
continue to receive nourishing meals while staying active and engaged—thanks to the
dedication of our transportation and operations teams. Come grow with us, as we remain
committed to serving and supporting our senior community. Inglewood Senior Center
Nutrition Department: (310) 412-5535. Senior Center Activities - On August 13th, we will
be showing the movie “My Big Fat Greek Wedding”. On August 14th, we will have a Luau
celebration from 10:00 a.m. – 11:00 a.m. with games and raffles prizes. On August 17th, LA
County of Mental Health will be conducting a presentation on “Social Isolation” from 10:45
a.m. – 11:45 a.m. On August 26th, we will have our monthly dance from 2:00 p.m. – 4:00

  4
   Park and Recreation Commission

p.m. In August we will be taking 15 seniors to two trips to the Redondo Beach Pier from
10:30 a.m. – 2:30 p.m. (dates - TBD).

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Park, Recreation and Community Services Assistant Director Teresa
Estrada reported on the following: Free LA Jazz Festival at Edward Vincent Park - The
Department of Parks, Recreation and Community Services was pleased to announce that
the LA Jazz Festival planned to present a free community concert at the Edward Vincent
Jr. Unfortunately; The Jazz Festival has been canceled. The event was scheduled to take
place on Saturday, August 8, 2026, from 3:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. This exciting event would
have featured an afternoon of outstanding live jazz performances by acclaimed artists,
including Cameron Graves, Harry the Nightgown, and the Michael Higgins Band. The
festival was designed to bring residents and visitors together through the enjoyment of
world-class music in a welcoming outdoor setting. Parks Building Groundbreaking
Ceremony - The Department is excited to share that construction of a new Parks
Maintenance Building at Edward Vincent, Jr. Park is moving forward. A Groundbreaking
Ceremony has been scheduled for Tuesday, August 25, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. This project
represents a significant investment in the City's parks infrastructure and a major milestone
for the Department. The existing maintenance building has served the City for many years
and is in need of replacement. The new facility will provide a modern, safe, and efficient
workspace for Parks staff, enhancing the Department's ability to maintain and improve our
parks and recreational facilities. Mayor James T. Butts, Jr., members of the City Council,
City staff, and community leaders are expected to participate in this important event.
Demolition of the existing building and construction of the new facility are anticipated to
begin during the 2027 Fiscal Year. We warmly invite our Commissioners to attend this
historic occasion as we celebrate the beginning of an exciting new chapter for our Parks
Department. Annual Family Unity Day - The Department is pleased to support the Annual
Family Unity Day, hosted by Councilwoman Gloria D. Gray, on Saturday, August 29, 2026,
from 12:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. at Darby Park, 3400 W. Arbor Vitae Street, Inglewood. Family
Unity Day is one of Inglewood's signature community events, bringing together families,
neighbors, and local organizations for an afternoon of fellowship, entertainment, and
community engagement. The event will feature live musical performances, complimentary
food, games and activities for children, community resource booths, and a variety of
family-friendly attractions. This free event reflects the City's commitment to strengthening
community relationships and promoting healthy, active lifestyles for residents of all ages.
Everyone is encouraged to attend, and we extend a special invitation to our Commissioners
to join us in celebrating this wonderful community tradition.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

  5
   Park and Recreation Commission

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Denmon invited the new Commissioners,
Commissioner Quinones (District 2) and Commissioner Monge (District 3) to visit the parks
to be acquainted.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:28 p.m.
